The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 13:21 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Members,
(13:21 hrs)
The proceedings commence. Honourable Members, each Honourable Member has been allocated 1 minute to speak during Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina.

Honourable Member Goma Devi Timalsina
(Nepali Communist Party): - Right Honourable
(13:21 hrs)
Chairperson,
Although the time is short, I am happy to be able to speak. There are many incidents of murder and robbery happening these days. Women sleeping at home have their earrings snatched and are left bleeding. Incidents like looting women going to graze cattle in the jungle, and murder and kidnapping of small children are increasing. I request the government, through the Honourable Chairperson, to control this as soon as possible. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Durga Gurung.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Member Durga Gurung (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable Chairperson,
(13:23 hrs)
932
The tower between Deurali and Chisapani of the 132 KV transmission line was felled by a storm, and power is being supplied from the old 33 KV line. Currently, due to the disruption of the 132 KV transmission line, there is very low voltage in Surkhet and surrounding areas, and even electrical appliances are not working. It is said that the construction of the 132 KV tower is underway, but it is expected to take one to two months. I would like to draw the attention of the government, through the Honourable Chairperson, to take necessary initiatives to expedite the construction work as soon as possible. Thank you. Jai Nepal.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Narayan Datta Mishra.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Member Narayan Datta Mishra (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable
(13:24 hrs)
Chairperson,
Sir, it is not appropriate to discuss much about the judiciary here. However, the judiciary is independent, and it is the responsibility of the executive and legislature to keep it independent and impartial. The Acting Chief Justice ordered the Supreme Court administration to immediately register the pending writ petitions on Monday. However, allegations are being made that the Supreme Court administration has obstructed justice by not registering some writ petitions after the recommendation of the new Chief Justice. Yesterday, immediately after that, the incident of high-ranking officials of the justice administration leaving their posts has caused turmoil in the country's justice system. The turmoil in the country's justice system is increasing day by day, and on the other hand, the Bar Association has decided to hold a program today to search for justice, conscience, and fair process by lighting a lantern. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar (Nepali Communist Party): - Right Honourable
(13:26 hrs)
Chairperson,
The settlement of the landless is like a battlefield after the war. In the shelter, the cries of the elderly, nursing mothers, pregnant women, sick children, and children who were driven out of their huts in the rain, their tears flowing continuously, whose heart would not melt at such a cry? How cruel is the government, the arrogance of two-thirds majority, towards humanity? Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Mohammad Khalid.
(13:27 hrs)
Honourable Member Mohammad Khalid (People's Socialist Party, Nepal): - Right Honourable
(13:27 hrs)
Chairperson, in point number 2 of the principles and priorities of the presented Appropriation Bill, 2023, it is stated that we are in the process of budget formulation with equal opportunities in mind. This is welcome and commendable. Because without providing equal opportunities along with equal rights, equal rights remain meaningless. In this regard, I would like to request that the government provide ownership to madrasas and madrasa education, respecting the objective of madrasa establishment, and provide facilities in the budget of 2083/084 in a timely manner. It is also very important to connect madrasas with digital technology. For that, I request the provision of infrastructure, technology, materials, and skilled manpower.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma.
(13:28 hrs)
Honourable Member Yuvraj Sharma (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable Chairperson, yesterday
(13:28 hrs)
there was a plight of the poor on the footpath, and today it is the plight of the landless. Similarly, tomorrow, under the guise of amendment, will the current constitution itself be in disarray? There is apprehension everywhere. Furthermore, everyone is worried that Saturn Dev Risai might lock up the institution and leave with the key. The situation of the Supreme Court is evident. Right Honourable Chairperson, it seems the government prefers the words 'rule' and 'administration' over 'service' and 'justice', and the former king over citizens. Is there a hidden motive behind changing the name of the East-West Highway and spreading rumors about the five development regions? We MPs are currently enduring the outbreak of silence, but it will be difficult for the Nepali people to endure the potential outbreak of Ebola. Through the Right Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to this. Finally, I would like to advise the learned Honourable Finance Minister not to make himself light by boasting about the 7 percent economic growth rate. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire.
(13:29 hrs)
Honourable Member Rajendra Laxmi Gaire (Nepali Communist Party): - Right Honourable
(13:30 hrs)
Chairperson, we knew that the Ministry of Home Affairs had been with the Prime Minister for a long time. Today, news has come that the army has been mobilized to collect data on how many landless people are in villages and settlements across the country. Hearing this news, many people have become destitute. People are crying now. There is fear and terror elsewhere. Today, the Prime Minister, who should be a guardian of the nation, has created an environment of fear and terror among the people. The government should think about this seriously and let the people live peacefully. I want to draw the government's attention to this matter. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.
(13:31 hrs)
Honourable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepali Communist Party): - Right Honourable
(13:31 hrs)
Chairperson, technology has developed a lot. In this context, the idea of Nepal becoming digitized and paperless has also emerged. This is not a bad thing at all. But I sometimes wonder if this is possible in a country like Nepal. Just recently, one Honourable Member experienced the state of our technology. If this continues, what will happen when the entire country becomes digitized? Will we have to go back to paper again? Therefore, our rulers must pay attention to ensuring that we do not have to step back and go back to the past, but always move forward. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa.
(13:32 hrs)
Honourable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML): -
(13:32 hrs)
Chairperson, in the Likhu Pike rural municipality area of Solukhumbu district, three hydropower projects that are being built and have been built have not followed the EIA report, have not fulfilled their legal obligations as per social responsibility, and have not followed the rules for the distribution of shares to local project-affected people. Therefore, through the Honourable Chairperson, I draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to fulfill its obligations in that area. Thank you.

Right Honourable Chairperson: - Honourable Members,
The process of Honourable Members speaking during Zero Hour concludes here.

(13:32 hrs)
Honourable Members, a letter regarding the assignment of portfolios of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers has been received from the office. I will now inform you of the contents of the letter.

Honourable Minister of Health and Population, Nisha Mehta, has departed for Geneva, Switzerland, on May 2, 2083, to participate in the World Health Assembly and Executive Board meeting. In her absence, the portfolio of the Ministry of Health and Population, which she has been managing, will be handled by the Honourable Minister of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation, Pratibha Rawal, as assigned by the Right Honourable Prime Minister. This is for your information.

Suman Raj Aryal,
Chief Secretary
May 4, 2083.

Honourable Members, the discussion on the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill for the fiscal year 2083/084, excluding the tax proposals, will continue.

Honourable Members, I will provide time to the remaining speakers according to the list of names received for participation in the discussion on a party basis. First, Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini, time 10 minutes. Following this, Honourable Member Urmila Aryal.

Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress): - Right Honourable
(13:34 hrs)
Chairperson,
Sir, the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, 2083, presented by the Honourable Finance Minister, have some positive aspects. Nepal's constitution pays attention to democratic values, principles, and ideals of good governance, justice, employment-oriented ideals, and the spirit of maintaining quality service. The upcoming budget, which mentions good governance being carried out by citizens through direct methods and legislative means, aims to transform the economy into a productive economy by saving citizens' time and effort, and it is mentioned that entrepreneurship will be managed. The principle of instilling confidence in the private sector is also mentioned. Education, health, skills, equal access, and other such aspects can be considered positive in these principles and priorities. However, the work being done by the government does not inspire confidence that these principles and priorities will be implemented.

The executive branch has been managing the legislative branch. The parliament session was called by the Right Honourable President upon recommendation, and the parliament was convened. The next day, it was recommended to postpone it again, and ordinances were brought by circumventing the session. Similarly, the Honourable Prime Minister does not seem to be positive towards the Honourable Members elected by the people and the parliament. Is this good governance? They are also pursuing a policy of interference towards the judiciary. Breaking the tradition of recommending the senior-most judge, recommending a junior judge for Chief Justice is interference in the judiciary, in my opinion.

Right Honourable Chairperson, Sir, while some are facing death and misfortune, others are accumulating wealth. Today, the landless are in extreme pain. They have been rendered homeless. Without any compassion for children, the elderly, the weak, and the sick, they have been made homeless without prior notice.

6. Because of that, I feel like a citizen of a country without humanity. The time for the year to start again is approaching. I want to draw the government's attention through this respected house to arrange food and shelter for them. Respected Chairperson, the private sector's confidence was established, and it was mentioned as a priority, but in practice, the current government has been suppressing and intimidating the private sector. Therefore, the private sector is currently in a state of despair. Isn't the private sector the one that pays 80 percent of the revenue and provides employment to many? If the private sector is attacked, it can lead to a great curse for the country in the coming days. I support the points raised by our honorable members that many things that should be principles and priorities have been missed. But today, the public is suffering from the high prices of petrol, diesel, kerosene, gas, and food grains. They are in distress. Is it acceptable for the government to remain silent? Similarly, the government is also silently allowing the adulteration and sale of food items connected to the daily lives of the public. I want to draw the government's attention to starting the work of good governance from itself. Finally, 'The slogan of good governance is corruption, the practice does not seem to be implemented. First, reform yourself and become clean to eradicate corruption. A new path of good governance will be formed.' Thank you, Jai Nepal. May everyone be victorious, Jai Nepal. Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Urmila Aryal, time 7 minutes. (13:40 hrs) After this, Honorable Member Somnath Poudel. Honorable Ms. Urmila Aryal (Communist Party of Nepal): Respected Chairperson (13:41 hrs) Madam, I want to express some views regarding the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, 2083. The Finance Minister has spoken on many aspects, including transforming the consumption-based economy into an investment and production-oriented economy. Overall, many things are inconsistent or lack significant coordination. The direction is not clear, and the guidance is not clear. There are also many lapses in the vision. In terms of income distribution, the top ten percent have 24.2 percent, and the bottom ten percent have only 3.7 percent income. According to this calculation of wealth share distribution, Nepal is very rich in terms of assets; the top 1 percent own 24 percent of the wealth, and the poorest 50 percent own only 4.4 percent of the wealth. Now, looking at gross fixed capital formation, infrastructure, schools, hospitals, things that last more than a year and have an overhead period. Therefore, depreciation also occurs in this regard. To increase the economic growth rate by 1 percent, it is necessary to increase it by about 6 percent. And to increase the economic growth rate by 6 percent of GDP, the investment rate needs to be increased by about 42 percent, right? So, looking at this, the principles and priorities of this budget are unlikely to succeed as stated. The current target of increasing Gross Fixed Capital Formation from 24 percent to 42 percent for capital formation, where is the plan to achieve it? A plan should have been made, and investment should have been made. It should have been formed in that way. The plan to increase the capital output ratio is not clearly visible. It is lacking, or it is not there at all. Even if it exists, some say it doesn't. Similarly, it is not clear how these principles and priorities align with the Sustainable Development Goals or our long-term development goals. It is also unclear how these principles and priorities align with the constitution's directive principles of a socialist-oriented system. Similarly, marginalized communities, Dalits, the Raute community, minority communities, and backward communities are not addressed by the principles and priorities. Although Nepal's economy relies on remittances and agriculture, there is silence on the aspect of adequate promotion. There is a need for adequate promotion in this regard. There is a need to increase investment in agriculture. It appears silent on this. Similarly, in the context of agriculture at the basic level in Nepal, no concrete plan has been proposed in the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill. That is lacking. It does not seem to be in a way that achieves the goals for youth self-employment for Dalit and marginalized communities. Therefore, overall, youth self-employment, marginalized communities, Dalit communities. Similarly, with the Raute people, will they always be kept as Raute? Right? Their habitat, their education, their settlement. Arranging marriages for young girls with old men, in terms of culture, it is like coercion. That needs to be improved. There is a need to bring such policies. Basically, in the Terai, the Dom community is considered untouchable. They are very backward in education. These communities are not addressed by these principles and priorities at all. In terms of the economy, in terms of the rural economy, how can we bring them into full infrastructure? This is not addressed by our principles and priorities. Clear provisions for infrastructure development and production increase have not been made. Looking at it this way, the Finance Minister is very learned. He is also very knowledgeable. But perhaps because he has studied extensively in favor of a capitalist economy, he has not paid attention to the matters that should be mentioned in the principles and priorities for a country like ours, and the marginalized communities, and the principles and priorities he has put forth are not realistic, practical, and implementable, in my opinion. Thank you. Respected Chairperson: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel, time 8 minutes. (13:46 hrs) After this, Honorable Member Mahanta Thakur. Honorable Mr. Somnath Poudel (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Respected Chairperson Madam, I would like to express my sincere gratitude and thanks for providing time to discuss the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill presented by the Honorable Finance Minister in the House. I participated in the discussion today after seeking suggestions from friends on social media yesterday. A learned friend sent me a suggestion via inbox. He said about the principles and priorities of this Appropriation Bill, "It has the address of heaven written on it, but the path to get there does not lead to heaven." Taking inspiration from my friend's words, I want to remind the government that we must not take steps towards hell while holding the address of heaven in our hands. I want to remind the government to keep this in mind. Chairperson Madam, looking at the main headings of the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill, as my learned friend commented, the address of heaven is abundant, but the destination cannot be reached. What are the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill based on? The directive principles of the constitution, fundamental rights, the Tenth Five-Year Plan, or something else? It is not clear. Our constitution ensures a socialist-oriented economy, inclusive, just, and balanced regional development, and economic equality, prosperity, and social justice. But that document, the document presented by the Finance Minister, does not contain those subjects even after searching and flipping through it many times. What happened? I don't know. Chairperson Madam, good governance is mentioned as a principle of the Appropriation Bill. The globally recognized aspects of good governance are the rule of law, accountability, transparency, responsibility, integrity, etc. While presenting the principle of this Appropriation Bill, the government has also formulated a new principle. A new principle of governance based on discretion. We have been continuously observing the government's actions. For the past 43 days, the government has shown us governance based on discretion by running bulldozers over the huts of citizens who have been living there for thirty years. Furthermore, the bulldozer stopping when it reached the house of a ruling party MP has also exposed the government's governance based on discretion. On the other hand, while talking about the supremacy of public integrity for good governance, we are also witnessing the government's integrity. Taking a cue from the words of the Honorable Finance Minister's past remarks, I want to ask the government. Does this government have the courage to investigate the assets of the members of this golden cabinet? I want to ask. Can this government make public the details of the service, facilities, and assets of the ministers and advisors appointed by the Prime Minister, and the members of their private secretariat? Respected Chairperson Madam, the government has also talked about restructuring the economy. I want to ask the Honorable Finance Minister, what is the roadmap for the government's fiscal federalism? What is the criterion for resource distribution to the provinces and local levels? Is the development of the revenue capacity of the provinces and local levels among the government's priorities or not? I want to ask the government. Chairperson Madam, while talking about restructuring, the government has also talked about creating an investment-friendly economic environment and restoring the confidence of the private sector. Chairperson Madam, a word is quite popular in society right now. The word 'kharaane gyaad' (ash gang) is popular. People say that the leaders of the 'kharaane gyaad' are currently in power. I don't know if what those people say is true or not. It is the government's responsibility to clarify when citizens ask questions, so I will not go into that. But I want to tell the government this: an investment-friendly environment will not be created by setting fire to industries. The confidence of the private sector will not be restored by arbitrarily arresting and detaining industrialists and businessmen. I want to ask the government: is it the government's responsibility to compensate for the damage to industries and citizens' private property that have been turned into ashes? I want to ask. Respected Chairperson Madam, another subject is mentioned in the principles of the upcoming budget: the development of the general public and the middle class. The Honorable Finance Minister has informed us about this. I want to remind the Honorable Finance Minister, didn't you climb the ladder of power singing the song "No one speaks for the poor Chamelis"? I want to ask the government. When will landless poor citizens receive land? I want to ask the government. When will the 11,000-plus citizens from 2,616 families displaced by bulldozers running over citizens' huts receive houses? I want to ask the government. When will landless citizens across the country receive land? When will homeless citizens receive houses? I want to ask the government. When will the more than 800 children who cannot go to school because you demolished houses and schools be able to go to school? I want to ask. When and how will more than 700 critically ill patients receive medication and treatment? When will children, senior citizens, and lactating mothers receive hot meals and warm clothes? I want to ask the government.

Respected Chairperson, does the ruling party remember the manifesto it made during the election? I want to ask the government. Where has the promise to apologize for the discrimination and oppression done by the state to the oppressed Dalit community within 15 days of government formation and announce reform programs gone? When will those 15 days of government formation arrive, I want to ask the government. Let alone the government's promises, the body of Shri Krishna Bishwakarma from Sindhuli, who died in custody after being arrested by the government for the crime of marrying a non-Dalit, has been lying unclaimed at the Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu for a month. His family is begging the government for justice, including a judicial inquiry and punishment for the culprits. The Home Minister of the government is sleeping with oil in his ears. When will that ear oil run out and when will the government's ears open? I want to ask the government. The time to start is near. Paddy, one of the main crops of agriculture, Chairperson, is it or is it not a priority for this government to provide relief to the farmers? I want to ask. The government that ascended to power, after reaching power, it seems to have remembered the youth. Is the program targeting the youth, production and entrepreneurship programs, and subsidized loans for startups a priority for the government or not? Will the skills of the youth returning from foreign employment be utilized or not? I want a clear answer from the government. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mr. Mahanth Thakur, time 5 minutes. (1:54 PM) After this, Honorable Member Mr. Basudev Ghimire. Honorable Mr. Mahanth Thakur (Democratic Socialist Party, Nepal):- (1:54 PM) Respected Chairperson, there is a saying that 'there is no happiness in dreams when one is dependent.' When one is dependent, there is no happiness even in dreams. We don't know what the situation is when awake. We are all in this society. What kind of dreams are coming. If we are suffering in dreams, then perhaps you are not. But I think if you are, it's fine. Because my identity is of different kinds. I am also Madhesi. If you call me Nepali, then I am Nepali too. I have all identities, internal and external. That's why I know about some activities. Why did I wear this suit today? Because Gyanendra is the king of Janakpur. He tried to meet me many times. So today, by wearing this, I thought maybe he would remember, maybe he would meet me, so I came here wearing this black suit. Now let's see when he will meet. Thank you. Presiding Officer:- Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Lila Kumari Bhandari. (1:57 PM) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mr. Basudev Ghimire, time 10 minutes. (1:57 PM) After this, Honorable Member Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Honorable Mr. Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson, Honorable Members. I am standing here to discuss the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill 2023. Honorable Members, when we entered politics, we understood that for the service of the people, to make the poor people who have no shelter, who cannot afford medical treatment, who cannot afford education, like us, with the objective of BP Koirala's words in mind, we entered politics. BP Koirala had told the then King Mahendra in 2015/2016. When the then King Mahendra asked, "What is your plan?" he had said, "If I get to hold the reins of power for 15 years like me, my goal, my thinking is to create a middle-class family like me," BP Koirala had said. Similarly, BP Koirala had said, while attending a meeting of the Planning Commission, "Don't just put photos of the King and Prime Minister here, put a photo of a farmer plowing the field and then make plans." I am remembering that vividly today. Our Finance Minister is very learned and lives in the city. He has given priority to urban-centric principles rather than rural-centric ones. I feel this is the case in this Appropriation Bill. The constitution itself states that we will move forward with a socialist-oriented system and economic development. But from point 1 to point 40, the economic condition of the poor will improve. I did not find any plan that would improve the economic condition, and in the name of the middle class population, I feel this bill is oriented towards capitalism rather than socialism. For this, I want to draw the attention of the government through the Honorable Chairperson and attract the attention of the Finance Minister. We had the plan to move from a least developed country to a developing country by 2026, by 2027. When we cannot improve the economic status of the poor. We make plans sitting in a palace and make plans only for the protection and increase of the wealth of the capitalists, and that is our plan. Now, to move from a least developed country to a developing country by 2027, I feel that the principles and priorities for this are not given in this Appropriation Bill. Honorable Members, now let's talk about education. If education remains only traditional education, we cannot stop the migration of youth in this country. The youth who are going abroad. To stop them from going abroad, to stop them from going abroad, if we implement technical education from secondary schools to higher education and arrange for technical education that can provide employment within the country, it can provide great relief to many youths. The government, through social media, by doing nothing but opposing old parties in social media and throwing mud, has not been able to win the votes of the people on that basis. Not only that, what was the Gen Z movement for? It was for good governance and the people want nothing else. They want good governance for society. They want a corruption-free society. I don't see priority given here. I see point number 2 here. Good governance and justice, economic development of the country and quality public service. It is in this point. I feel like saying one thing here. And when the bulldozer was used on the poor and helpless people, was that good governance? I want to ask the government. Good governance means the protection of everyone's human rights, freedom of speech, the right to life, only when all these fundamental rights are protected will the people get the guarantee of good governance. By spreading terror, the government has ridiculed good governance. Even though this is written, it will only be a black scripture written in black letters on white paper inside a blue cover, like telling a story to a deaf person. Therefore, I want to say, the woman who was kept on a cot in Kohalpur, the woman who was kept under the bulldozer terror of the landless, whose children were crying "Mommy, Mommy" to the affected mother. If the wives and children of the ministers and prime ministers sitting in the government had been treated the same way, how would you have felt? Is that the bond of humanity? Can that be called good governance? What kind of good governance does the government seek? I want to ask the government. Now, in point number three, it is written, "Implement a series of administrative reforms to ensure that the direct benefits of good governance are felt in the daily lives of citizens." Whatever has been said is just ridiculous. Beautiful things are written. The scene of women, children, and men being dragged by armed police and police at the border while carrying goods worth one hundred rupees, have you definitely seen it on social media? You friends are very adept at social media. You are experts, friends in the government. Or friends from the independent party. Didn't it hurt you even a little to see that? Didn't you feel any sensitivity? Don't you have any humanity? And you say that the old parties did nothing, we will do it. Now I want to ask you, you have started destroying the judiciary, you have started destroying universities, and where else are you planning to destroy things? You should tell us that too. All the roads that have been built, all the infrastructure that has been built in Nepal, all the infrastructure for education and health, all the infrastructure for tourism, have all been built by the old parties. We have built them. You are riding on them today. Don't cut short your dreams like this. You also need to consider this. You have formed a government that is close to a two-thirds majority, whether through wordplay or by winning the hearts of the people, by transforming within 4 years. But you do not understand what police brutality is, what torture in custody is, what torture in jail is... (Time expired) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member, time is up. After this, Honorable Member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar, time 9 minutes. Then Honorable Member Roshi Meche. Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party):- Respected Chairperson, although I am standing here to discuss the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill 2083, I do not have much enthusiasm. Respected Chairperson, why is that? Because this document, the Appropriation Bill 2083, is full of ingratitude and betrayal. This document lacks clear thought, strong thought, and strong ideology. It lacks clear political philosophy. Its gender is not clear. It is not known whether it is male or female. Even if it had a gender, we would have to accept it, but that is not the case either. The creator and presenter of this document, the Honorable Finance Minister, has already said that he is not a communist. Is he bourgeois? Is he reactionary? Is he capitalist? He has not said that. Therefore, its clear identity is not established, and similarly, it has not paid homage to the great martyrs. What kind of document is this? Respected Chairperson, I am not saying this out of thin air or baseless speculation. I want to present proof of this. What does it say in the first sentence, 'A capable, just, and prosperous Nepal, built on the foundation of the transformative movement and sacrifice of the youth of Nepal, with the complete aspirations of the general public, a government formed with an unprecedented mandate obtained through elections.' But what has it done for this movement-oriented youth class? Respected Gen Z class, you have been betrayed. I said in English yesterday, "You are betrayed." To borrow the words of Honorable Renu Chandra, I want to say in Nepali, "You have been betrayed." This entire document of 40 points, nowhere in it do I see any program focused on the youth class. This is one reason why I lack enthusiasm. There is no tribute to the martyrs. It only says, "I respectfully remember the martyrs who sacrificed their lives." Only remembering the martyrs? Yes, that's why I don't have much enthusiasm to speak about this document. But Respected Chairperson, the creator and presenter of this document is an internationally renowned scholar, an economist, and a representative of my constituency. Even though his house is not there...

Even if there is no one, no family, no organization or workers, they have been elected twice with a huge majority. This is a document prepared and presented by such a person. I have come here taking 9 minutes each. Therefore, I had to say something.

Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, I want to say something. The party that went to the election with a 100-point manifesto presented a 100-point policy and program. It presented that it would complete 100 programs in 100 days. But unfortunately, this bill has only 40 points. There are only 5 priorities and 4 principles. Perhaps that's why 60 points are missing from it, they are not here. Perhaps that's why many things are missing, many things are not mentioned here. The very first thing is that its principles and priorities are in disarray, chaotic, and upside down. Is it a principle or a priority, is it a priority or a program of principles, I don't know. There are many things here, but there is a time constraint. So I want to give just one example, soft power.

Soft power means diplomacy, identity, education, etc. Hard power means military, government, etc. What is this? Is this soft power a policy, a principle? Is it a program or a tool or a medium? This is not clear from the document. Similarly, it talks about establishing order. This document is presented with the art of establishing order. But what kind of order it is, I don't know. Is the formation of a golden cabinet this order? Similarly, 13 days after the formation of the cabinet, one minister is gone, 24 days later another minister is gone, after 4/5 days, reshuffling of seniority, bulldozer terror, the session called by the Honorable President at their recommendation, adjournment of the session. Why? To bring an ordinance. Similarly, the report prepared by themselves, the policy and program, while being presented by the Honorable President, the Honorable Prime Minister was absent, there was a lack of presence, absence. (17:04 PM)
Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle to respond to the questions raised in the discussion on the principles and priorities of the Appropriation Bill for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, excluding the tax proposal.
Honorable Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle:- Honorable Chairperson, I express my respect on behalf of the government for the views, suggestions, and queries expressed in this esteemed house yesterday and today. We believe in pluralistic democracy. We respect differing opinions. "Vade Vade Jayate Tattvabodh" - knowledge and understanding are born from continuous discussion. We are all bound by the common goal of nation-building. If we separate means and ends, perhaps our disagreements may also seem artificial to a large extent. Our common destination is a well-governed, prosperous Nepal. The size of the economy should increase, there should be an increase in respectable employment and average per capita income. The state's capacity to invest in social justice should increase. International competition and self-respect should be maintained. The destination is this, the end is this, but the path to reach there is different, it has been different. That is why the Rastriya Swatantra Party was born. The path is different. The path is different. Not means and ends. The end is the same. Therefore

If we proceed with a slightly different approach, and if the policies, governance style, and character of the past 30 years had been appropriate, there would not have been such strong demands for generational change in politics and transformation in the economic and social sectors. In the last three decades, Nepal, Nepali citizens, and the overall economy have paid a heavy price for misgovernance. I have often mentioned the lost economic opportunities, employment, and potential economic growth, referred to as 'missing GDP,' due to slow decision-making processes, collusion, policy uncertainty, the intermediary system, and institutional exploitation. This cost is unimaginable. That is precisely why we went to the public with a commitment to establish good governance and brought it back approved by the people as a manifesto. This approved concept and framework are now reflected in the government's policy and programs, the principles and priorities of the appropriation bill, the government's 100-point roadmap for governance reform, the common commitment, and will also be in the upcoming budget. That is the most sacred document for us. I wish to inform this esteemed house that our governance journey for the next five years will proceed on that foundation. I humbly request that you revisit the old jargon and the documents you yourself have been writing and speaking about. Elections have consequences. We are committed to the constitution. And I mentioned this baseless suspicion in this esteemed house the previous time as well. It is truly regrettable to be compelled to repeat it. We have participated in the elections by accepting the concept envisioned by this very constitution. And this constitution itself has provided the steps to amend it, even if there are things within it that are not liked, by taking recourse to Articles 274 and 275 and following the necessary legal procedures. It is precisely because this constitution has such provisions that we have embarked on the current journey. Therefore, we are committed to building a society that is equitable and inclusive. We are dedicated to equality of opportunity and the secure expansion of the middle class. When terms, words, and concepts that have been learned and studied are not immediately apparent, and some honorable members have argued that this might indicate a wavering commitment to the constitution or a deviation from the goals of an equitable society, I want to assure this esteemed house, through the honorable Chairperson, that this is unnecessary. If you revisit our documents, you will see that the language of our state's guiding principles, our sustainable development goals, and our various periodic plans are consistent with this. I have also brought with me the budget presented by the respected Suvarna Shumsher in the year 2008 BS. At that time too, the goal was to improve the standard of living of the citizens. Therefore, the language of 75 years ago, the current language, and the language the state will speak in 50 years will all be the same. It will encompass education, health, governance reform, and infrastructure. However, the style, form, and character will evolve. Even in the United States, the world's largest economy, today's debates are about education, health, social security, infrastructure, and defense. Therefore, the form evolves, but my humble submission is that dissecting the words in this manner is somewhat superficial. We need to get to the core, to the essence, to the spirit. Only then will we be united again in that common destination. We have taken a different path, and that different path has been approved, bringing us here. Some honorable members have also inquired about the main priorities. Our top priority is good governance. Our belief is that sustainable economic growth is impossible without good governance. Corruption, delays, the intermediary system, and the illegal capture of institutions have not only increased the cost of the state but also weakened public trust. Therefore, this government is moving forward on the path of economic reform through system improvement. Provisions like e-governance, digital delivery, one-time data submission, and performance contracts are not just about technology. They are the basis for transforming the culture of state operation and changing mindsets. We have envisioned a state that delivers, not just spends. The principles and priorities of this appropriation bill have also come about in that context. Some honorable members have expressed concerns that the private sector is hesitant and losing confidence. The government will not shy away from calling out wrongdoing and stopping it. Our main objective is to free the state from the cycle of cronyism, policy capture, and exploitation and to deliver the benefits of good governance to all citizens. There is complete consistency between our thinking, policies, programs, and the principles and priorities of the appropriation bill. The upcoming budget will also be in that direction. I heartily urge our honorable friends in the opposition to be constructive partners in this journey of change, not obstacles. Please alert us if we overstep. But please refrain from supporting those who engage in malfeasance under the guise of private enterprise and exhibit criminal tendencies. Some honorable members have commented on the concept of expanding the middle class. Clarification is needed here. Expanding the middle class does not mean providing benefits to a select few. Its main objective is to uplift the economic status of the poor, laborers, farmers, landless, squatters, and disadvantaged communities. We do not believe in the equal distribution of poverty. We operate on the principle that we must lift the poor to create a broader middle class. Only when citizens' income, skills, productivity, and access to opportunities increase will genuine social mobility, upward mobility, and upward social mobility be possible. Therefore, this concept links social justice with economic upliftment. This is a new concept we have introduced. Many honorable members commented last time that the policy and program were too old. Now, based on the same policy and program, I have also observed objections being raised in both houses that there is nothing old in the principles and priorities presented. I humbly reiterate: the state is not a temporary political structure. It is an institution of continuous succession. The Nepali state has been functioning since 1769. Political figures like us come and go, but the state continues. We have embraced the concept of that institution of continuous succession. We have honored and are carrying the immense responsibilities imposed upon us even before we came into power. Even if the money is insufficient, we have honored the obligations undertaken by previous governments by finding resources and making sacrifices. This is not out of any special affection for previous governments. We have carried the concept of the state's continuity, its sanctity. Therefore, the name of the main subject is not important. What matters is the perspective, the style of implementation, and the expected results. How we view those sectors, how we implement them, and what results citizens achieve are the real differences. If honorable members could analyze with a slightly different perspective, delving into the depth of the documents rather than deviating, it would further assist the government. Many honorable members have raised the issue of implementation, which is valid. It is valid to question. While the linguistic presentation is logical, the old suspicion of whether it will be implemented has been reiterated. I would like to add a few points regarding that. Any budget, policy program, or development vision is first clearly written. Then, the first condition for good implementation is clear thinking, writing, and accountability. This document has been prepared with implementation at its center. In fact, for this reason, we have placed special emphasis on an 'implementation architecture' in this year's principles and priorities. We are well aware that citizens are now looking for results, not speeches. We have placed legal reform, institutional accountability, timelines, digital tracking, direct monitoring, and outcome measurement at the center of state operation, and we have also named this 'mission mode.' To save time, I will not elaborate on its explanation now, but I humbly request the honorable members, through the honorable Chairperson, to understand the government's momentum over the past 40 days as being inspired by this 'mission mode' thinking. Therefore, I submit that this is not a change of words. It is a new experiment in governance philosophy and an execution model. The five guiding principles we have presented are: the dividends of good governance, economic restructuring, integrated infrastructure for resilience, social investment, and multidimensional international relations. Priorities have been formulated based on these. We believe these priorities will bring qualitative improvements in economic growth, employment, social justice, productivity, competitiveness, and the standard of living of citizens. Honorable members of the National Assembly have raised some specific issues. I wish to address them briefly. Regarding the issue that programs to retain youth in the country are not visible, we highly value the contribution of youth, including Gen Z. The integration of the education system with production, entrepreneurship, innovation, and the labor market is mentioned in point number 10. There is a significant emphasis on technical education, and we will allocate budgets accordingly to make it reliable. Regarding the agricultural sector and the upliftment of the farmer class, honorable members have shown interest. In point number 20, we have included issues related to agricultural fertilizer, seeds, irrigation, support prices, and overall price reforms. Developing sectors like agriculture, energy, and tourism as economic value chains is mentioned in point number 21. I briefly touched upon the role of the private sector earlier, but we consider the private sector as the leader of economic development. Expanding investment in new industries like energy and green hydrogen is in point 22. We have made increasing the confidence of the private sector a mandatory condition. Point number 22 also mentions bringing dozens of investment-friendly laws. On the day I became Finance Minister, I abolished 15 outdated laws that were hindering private enterprise, and we will announce dozens more such laws through the budget, and we will continue this economic chain in this session. If physical infrastructure development does not involve private sector partnership beyond the government's balance sheet, then none of our big goals – expressways, dry ports, tunnels, overpasses, underpasses – will be possible. Therefore, for the first time this year, we have moved forward with attracting private capital from beyond the government's balance sheet in the budget, and the current principles and priorities also state the goal of concentrating the government's scarce resources in backward communities like Karnali, Sudurpaschim, and Madhesh.

It is about the spirit of federalism. Policy point number 13 mentions strengthening the cooperative federal system. The problem of savings is clearly addressed in point number 36, with a long-term solution for the problem of savings, and its process has also started since yesterday. The Ministry of Finance has allocated 25 crore rupees this year. We are ready to allocate an additional 24 crore rupees, and the Ministry of Cooperatives has advanced this work. And this is not money borrowed from the state treasury. We do not distribute from that. Relying on cooperatives, by selling assets from the fund, a process is starting for savings to go to the savers, but due to the time lag of liquid and illiquid assets, the government has only provided temporary facilitation. The development of a production-oriented economy is clearly written in points number 4, 6, etc. I humbly request that points number 36 and 37 be read in full regarding social justice, Dalits, and marginalized communities. The issues of Madhesh and Karnali are also clearly written in point number 38. The transformation of regions including Madhesh, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim is a top priority of the state. I have found one thing: when the words that the honorable members have known, read, and mentioned in their speeches are not immediately seen, it seems they are under the illusion that it has not been done. Now, one thing must be accepted. The path is different. Our manifesto was a bit different, and based on that approved manifesto, we have given concrete shape to these concepts in the state's valid documents. I humbly request this. The upliftment of the lower class below the middle class should be the state's priority, and the state is the support for the poor, but if we cannot expand the size and scope of the middle class, this democracy will not survive, and we will not be able to do justice to the traditional standards of development. Therefore, I have emphasized these points. I have concluded that the honorable members have not even read about finding sustainable sources for the new fund. In point number 23, alternative development, infrastructure, forests, green forests, search for financial sources, and the concept I mentioned earlier, if we do not look for sources outside the government's balance sheet, we will not be able to spend capital. This year, with only 2 months left in the fiscal year, we have spent only 1 crore out of a capital budget of 4 crore. In an economy of 66 crore, the government has invested only 1 crore in capital expenditure. Where will we reach with that? We will not reach anywhere, and in terms of achieving big goals like economic growth and increasing the size of the economy, we also have a large private sector outside the government. Domestic, expatriate, and foreign. Their capital must be brought in. And the government is ready to provide the commitment and policy commitment required for that. I have stated that issues like good governance and fiscal transparency are guiding principles for the upcoming budget. I would like to inform you that public service delivery has been addressed through the emphasis on digitalization to maintain budgetary good governance. It has been raised in the National Assembly that emphasis should be placed on the use of electrical appliances to address the current petroleum crisis. Priority for the development of renewable energy is in point number 27. Mass transit system, electric mass transit system in major cities including Kathmandu Valley is in point number 29. The issue of management of landless and squatters is written in point number 37. We have also made a strong commitment regarding the comprehensive restructuring of health insurance. We will do this in point number 35. Because last year, the health insurance allocated 10 billion rupees has a current liability exceeding 30 billion rupees. The liability for agricultural fertilizer, which was allocated 28 billion rupees, has now reached 66 billion rupees. We cannot bear this. We want to move forward by making fundamental reforms in these areas, and the budget will address it. Periodic plans and international agreements are guiding principles. We believe in the continuity of the state, and the principles of the appropriation bill clearly speak about these matters. The Ministry of Finance is working on bringing closed industries back into operation. Due diligence audit of seven sick industries is about to be completed, and based on their recommendations and professional advice, we will present how to move them forward. The government will not run them, but we will advance them through the PPP model. The restructuring of public institutions is also mentioned in point number 23. I have already informed you about the commitment to complete incomplete projects. To resolve legal and procedural problems seen in the implementation of large projects, we will allocate the budget in a results-oriented manner, similar to the mission mode I discussed earlier, by signing performance agreements with project chiefs and completing national priority projects within a specified time. We will also address the reconstruction of infrastructure damaged during the movement with concrete provisions in the budget and programs. The Ministry of Finance is honoring this. I would like to inform the honorable members through the honorable Chairperson that the budget is being released. Honorable Chairperson, the principles and perspectives of the appropriation bill we have presented do not just represent the government's guiding priorities. I urge this honorable house to accept it as a commitment in an honest effort to also reflect the constitutional directive principles, national plans, and other matters. Finally, the government will seriously consider the important ideas raised here. I call upon everyone to make the discussion related to nation-building mature and result-oriented, expecting deeper study, foresight, and constructive suggestions from the honorable members. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson, the discussion on the proposal "Let the principles and priorities of the appropriation bill for the fiscal year 2083/084, excluding tax proposals, be discussed in the assembly" is concluded here. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that the suggestions expressed by the honorable members in the assembly regarding the principles and priorities of the appropriation bill for the fiscal year 2083/084, excluding tax proposals, will be integrated and sent to the Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers and the Ministry of Finance through the Secretariat. Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will be held on Friday, Jestha 8, 2083, at 1:15 PM, and this meeting is adjourned here. sections.summary_en: Several members raised concerns during Zero Hour. Goma Devi Timalsina spoke about rising crime and requested government intervention. Durga Gurung highlighted issues with the 132 KV transmission line affecting electricity supply. Narayan Datta Mishra discussed concerns regarding the judiciary and recent events in the Supreme Court. Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar described the plight of landless people. Mohammad Khalid praised the budget's focus on equal opportunities and requested support for madrasas. Yuvraj Sharma criticized government actions regarding landless evictions and the judiciary, and advised the Finance Minister. Rajendra Laxmi Gaire expressed concern over army deployment for landless data collection and the resulting fear. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar questioned the feasibility of digitalization in Nepal. Sonam Geljen Sherpa raised issues regarding hydropower projects in Solukhumbu.

Another member criticized the government for suppressing the private sector, highlighting its contribution to revenue and employment, and warned of dire consequences if it is harmed. Concerns were also raised about inflation and adulteration of food items, with a call for the government to start practicing good governance.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Urmila Aryal discussed the Appropriation Bill, 2083, criticizing its inconsistencies, lack of clear direction, and vision. She highlighted income and wealth disparities, the need for increased investment for economic growth, and the bill's failure to align with Sustainable Development Goals, the constitution's socialist orientation, and the needs of marginalized communities. She also pointed out the lack of focus on agriculture and youth employment.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Somnath Poudel critiqued the Appropriation Bill's principles and priorities, stating they promise 'heaven' but lack a clear path. He argued the bill fails to reflect the constitution's socialist-oriented economy and principles of social justice and balanced development. He questioned the government's commitment to good governance, citing recent actions and demanding an investigation into ministers' assets. He also raised concerns about fiscal federalism, private sector confidence, and the lack of support for landless citizens and displaced families.

The speaker also notes the absence of mention for marginalized communities like Madhesi, indigenous, tribal, and Muslim. Further points include the omission of Nijgadh International Airport and the unclear concept of 'social market economy', contrasting it with the focus on the middle class despite rhetoric about the poor.

While acknowledging some positive points like inclusivity and 'investment express', the speaker concludes that the document has significant flaws and needs correction.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Roshri Meche presents suggestions on the Appropriation Bill, 2083, finding it idealistic but unclear in implementation. The speaker notes ambitious goals without clear roadmaps or responsibilities, and a weak reality analysis by the government. Key concerns include the lack of concrete plans for job creation, stopping foreign migration, and supporting youth entrepreneurship, as well as inadequate prioritization of agriculture despite its importance.

speakers.topic: Critique of Appropriation Bill's idealism and implementation clarity

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker criticizes the bill's lack of clear metrics and strategies for good governance and corruption control. Concerns are raised about the weak financial model for federalism implementation and the lack of clear fund allocation bases for provinces and local levels. The speaker also highlights the government's failure to address citizen concerns regarding digital transformation, including cybersecurity, digital literacy in rural areas, and data privacy, despite the push for a 'Digital Nepal'.

speakers.topic: Critique of governance, federalism finance, and digital Nepal

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasizes the need for timely information and transparency, criticizing the lack of a public dashboard for government spending and budget implementation. The bill is also faulted for failing to prioritize making Nepal an education and health hub and attracting foreign students and medical tourism. Furthermore, the speaker expresses disappointment over the government's indifference to modernizing the judiciary and providing speedy justice, noting that this issue was also raised in the zero hour.

The lack of policy for reconstruction and rehabilitation is highlighted, along with the government's failure to address damage to the private sector, including industries and businesses. The speaker questions whether the government can dismiss these significant events as minor.

She criticizes the current practice of 'imprison first, then listen' and questions the government's direction, noting that many registered industries are not operating at full capacity.

She highlights the negative impact on private sector investors, leading to declining morale and economic hardship.
